correctness.rationale: Inspected all seven actual frozen files (RESULT.md, SLOGAN.txt, AUDIT.json, METADATA.json, REVIEW.md, VERIFICATION.md, verify.py), with Git blob IDs reconstructing exact expected source-tree SHA 59263e5401b8897a57b6541d067f007a20df85aa. Independently rebuilt the Tribonacci 2-factor language {00,01,02,10,20} under phi=(01,02,0); every phi^4(a) has length >=7, so six-factors are exhausted by fifth two-letter boundary images, yielding 13 distinct six-factors. Since pi(0)=100,pi(1)=101,pi(2)=10 have image length >=2, a binary factor of length <=11 can touch at most six consecutive images; exact B languages equal all factors of pi(L6(T)) plus the one exceptional initial prefix. Independently computed each complete length 1..11 factor set via this cover and a second different phi^3 six-window cover from the previously published October 25 result, and compared them with a long prefix only as corroboration. Obtained factor counts 2,4,..,22, P=[2,2,2,2,2,1,2,1,1,0,0], Q=[0,1,2,2,2,3,2,1,0,0,0], and r=[2,3,4,6,8,9,12,15,18,20,22]. Length 10 has exactly the submitted 20 distinct factors and no reversals; any longer pair would induce a length-ten reversed factor pair. External Theorem 5 establishes #L_n=2n for every n>=1, giving r(n)=2n-Q(n). This is an infinite logical reduction, not an inference from a finite sampled prefix. Only n>=1 and the fixed exact word are claimed; reversal without binary complementation.

value.rationale: The exact reversal-equivalence class spectrum is a natural standalone invariant introduced and actively studied in primary reflection-complexity literature. Its permanent sharp cutoff at n=10 distinguishes the absence of ALL reversal pairs from mere eventual absence of palindromes, and records a meaningful classification of a named 2n-complexity Rote word that is not complement-symmetric. This precise Q-vector and r(n) formula can serve as a reference example distinguishing different symmetry classes, despite very substantial overlap with the published P-spectrum and finite-cover method. The result is narrow and computationally inexpensive once the October 25 cover is known; no new general theorem, historical priority or major methodological advance is asserted.

final_claim: For Kimberling binary word B=0pi(phi^omega(0)), every n=1..9 has P=(2,2,2,2,2,1,2,1,1) and nonpalindromic reversal-pair Q=(0,1,2,2,2,3,2,1,0); P(n)=Q(n)=0 for all n>=10. Thus B has 15 palindromes and reflection complexity r_B(n)=2n-Q(n). The P/15 component is already published (October 25); the independently reviewed substantive increment is the exact Q/r spectrum and reversal-free cutoff n=10.
limitations: Earlier October 25 published P-spectrum and complete short-factor six-window cover are credited; only Q/r and the length-ten reversal-pair exclusion are new as a complete explicit result.
The novelty margin is modest because its finite enumeration is a short extra operation on the earlier full-language cover.
No assertion of exclusive priority, general Rote classification or automated formal verification.
